articles.title: BridgeInvest Provides $114M Refi for Robert Rivani ‘Concierge Office’ in Miami Beach
articles.narrative: Developer Robert Rivani has secured a $114.3 million refinancing package for The Rivani, a 165,170-square-foot office and retail complex in Miami Beach. The new debt, provided by BridgeInvest, will retire $38 million in existing renovation debt and cover leasing costs to stabilize the property. The asset, which is 83 percent leased, has been transformed into a 'concierge office' with hospitality-inspired amenities, demonstrating strong demand for a differentiated workplace experience.

data_points.notable_features: Features hospitality amenities including a full-service concierge, valet, spa and fitness area, meditation room, podcast studio, and speakeasy-style lounge.
data_points.project_notes: Property was acquired in 2024 for $62.5 million. Developer is seeking voter approval for a $50 million expansion to add 47,000 square feet above an existing parking garage, which would reduce parking spots from 712 to 387.

articles.title: Vaja Group Acquires Astoria Development Site at 24-41 31st Street for $26M
articles.narrative: Vaja Group has acquired a 29,638-square-foot development site in Astoria, Queens, for $26.39 million. The site, formerly a retail building, offers nearly 150,000 buildable square feet and is suitable for a 108-unit mixed-use development with additional retail space and parking. This acquisition, along with a previous purchase, was facilitated by New York City's 2022 31st Street–Hoyt Avenue rezoning, which created a new mixed-use corridor.

data_points.notable_features: Site offers nearly 150,000 buildable square feet and can accommodate 14,000 square feet of potential retail space and parking.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously a Staples location. The acquisition was made possible by New York City's 31st Street–Hoyt Avenue rezoning effort in 2022.

articles.title: Beer-Importing Holterbosch Family Offloads LIC Warehouse for $95M
articles.narrative: The Holterbosch family, former owners of a German beer importing and distribution business, has sold a warehouse property in Long Island City, Queens, for $95 million. The buyer is Ground Lease REIT, an affiliate of Montgomery Street Partners. The family had owned the property since 1968, and the sale comes a decade after the passing of the family patriarch.

data_points.notable_features: Located on the Long Island City waterfront, near the Eleventh Street Basin inlet of the East River, offering potential for future development.
data_points.project_notes: The property was held by the Holterbosch family since approximately 1968.

articles.title: Juanita’s Foods to Consolidate L.A. Production at 120K-SF Facility
articles.narrative: Juanita's Foods, an 80-year-old food manufacturer, is consolidating its Southern California production into a new 120,000-square-foot facility in Santa Fe Springs, CA. This move marks the first transaction supported by the 'Big 4' partnership, an economic development coalition formed by four Los Angeles County industrial cities to attract and retain businesses through coordinated incentives and expedited permitting. The company considered locations nationwide before deciding to remain in Southern California, citing the city's business approach and incentive package as key factors.

data_points.address: 13100 Arctic Circle, Santa Fe Springs, CA
data_points.project_notes: The facility was acquired by LBA Logistics in December 2019. Juanita's Foods sold a majority stake to Apex Capital in May 2025.

articles.title: Knighthead Lends $63M or Doral, Fla., Industrial Portfolio Buy
articles.narrative: Midtown Capital Partners secured $62.92 million in acquisition financing from Knighthead Funding for its $86 million purchase of a 13-property urban-infill industrial portfolio in Doral, FL. The portfolio, totaling 290,000 square feet across 13.33 acres, was acquired off-market from Wes Realty. The transaction highlights the strong demand and institutional interest in the small-bay industrial sector in South Florida, where vacancy rates are exceptionally low.

data_points.notable_features: Urban-infill, small-bay industrial portfolio located within a mile of Miami International Airport.
data_points.project_notes: The 13 properties were developed and assembled over the last 30 years.

articles.market_intelligence: South Florida's small-bay industrial market is experiencing strong demand with vacancy rates below 3 percent.

articles.title: JLL Arranges $154.1M in Financing for Six-Property Retail Portfolio Spanning Three States
articles.narrative: JLL Capital Markets has arranged $154.1 million in financing for a six-property retail portfolio totaling 1.3 million square feet across California, Arizona, and Georgia. The financing was secured for Kimco Realty Corp. and an institutional joint venture partner through institutional investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management. The portfolio boasts a 99% occupancy rate and a strong tenant mix, including several grocery anchors and national retailers, with a significant portion of investment-grade credit tenants.

data_points.notable_features: The portfolio is 99% occupied with a 4.6-year weighted average lease term and features grocery anchors. National tenants occupy approximately 76% of the portfolio's gross leasable area, with 46% of the tenant roster comprising investment-grade credit.

articles.title: Thompson Thrift Opens 276-Unit Apartment Property in Colorado Springs
articles.narrative: Thompson Thrift has opened Switch, a 276-unit multifamily community in Colorado Springs. The development, which received equity financing from Thompson Thrift 2023 Multifamily Development L.P., is situated on 11 acres within the Polaris Pointe development, a large retail complex. The property offers a range of unit features and community amenities designed to enhance resident living.

data_points.notable_features: Located within the 200-acre Polaris Pointe retail complex, units feature smart home capabilities and full-sized washers/dryers, and community amenities include a resort-style heated swimming pool and 24-hour fitness center.

articles.title: C.W. Driver Cos. Breaks Ground on $74M Middle School, Gym Facility in Malibu
articles.narrative: C.W. Driver Cos. has commenced construction on Phase II of the Malibu Middle and High School campus, a $74 million project for the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District. This phase includes a new middle school core building and a gymnasium facility, totaling 40,000 square feet. The project is expected to be completed in late 2028.

data_points.property_name: Malibu Middle and High School campus
data_points.notable_features: Phase II includes a middle school core building with special education and counseling spaces, a wellness center, media lab, food-service areas, and shaded outdoor spaces, alongside a gymnasium with a fitness studio and multi-sport court.

articles.title: BWE Arranges $48M Refinancing for 978,000 SF Industrial Property in DeKalb, Illinois
articles.narrative: BWE has arranged a $48 million fixed-rate refinancing for a 978,000-square-foot industrial logistics facility in DeKalb, Illinois. Griffin Capital secured the loan from Aegon, a life insurance company lender. The property is fully leased to a major tenant and features specialized chemical storage, aerosol rooms, cold storage, and containment floors.

data_points.notable_features: Building features specialized chemical storage and aerosol rooms, cold storage facilities, and containment floors.

articles.title: Lanoha developing 150,000-square-foot office building in Omaha’s Heartwood Preserve
articles.narrative: Lanoha is developing a 150,000-square-foot trophy office building, named The Row, within Omaha's Heartwood Preserve mixed-use development. The building will serve as the future headquarters for a prominent law firm. Construction is slated to begin in late 2027, with completion expected in early 2030, bringing a significant office presence to the district's urban center.

data_points.address: 145th Street and Canopy Avenue, Omaha, NE
data_points.notable_features: Modern architecture, elevated finishes, and contemporary amenities with direct access to dining, retail, and green spaces; located directly across from the 18-acre Heartwood Park.
data_points.project_notes: Construction expected to begin in late 2027.

CenterPoint Commercial Companies launches capital markets division based in Dallas

articles.title: Draper and Kramer brokers $99 million loan for acquisition of 724,400-square-foot shopping center in Skokie
articles.narrative: Draper and Kramer's Commercial Finance Group brokered a $99.55 million loan for Fairbourne Properties to acquire Village Crossing, a 724,400-square-foot retail center in Skokie, IL. The financing will also cover tenant improvement and leasing commission costs for new leases at the property, which is anchored by a grocery store, movie theater, and sporting goods retailer.

articles.title: Why Job Numbers Don’t Tell the Whole Story
articles.narrative: This article argues that headline job numbers alone do not provide a complete picture of the U.S. labor market, which is sending mixed signals. While August saw 162,000 jobs added, primarily in food services, local government, and healthcare, hiring remains sluggish, and small businesses report difficulty filling openings. The author highlights discrepancies such as declining employment among younger workers, particularly in AI-exposed occupations, and a persistent skills mismatch in manufacturing. For commercial real estate, this means that investment and development decisions should consider employment types, specific labor needs, and employer-attractive locations rather than just national job growth figures. The article concludes that a nuanced understanding of industry, occupation, worker age, company strategy, and geography is crucial for predicting demand across various property types.

articles.title: Transparency Is Becoming a Prerequisite for CRE Capital
articles.narrative: Transparency in commercial real estate has evolved from a measure of market maturity to a critical prerequisite for capital deployment, according to a new report by JLL. The "Global Real Estate Transparency Index, 2026" highlights that transaction volumes in the most transparent markets have significantly outpaced less transparent ones, attracting over 98% of global real estate capital. This increased transparency facilitates earlier price discovery and enables investors to better understand market dynamics, price assets, and deploy capital more efficiently, even in alternative sectors where data can be limited. The report also emphasizes the need for strengthened valuation methodologies, standardized reporting, and clearer communication of liquidity terms to support a broader investor base and help all market participants navigate risk and opportunity.

articles.title: Construction’s Growth Story Depends on What’s Being Built
articles.narrative: The U.S. construction market is experiencing a bifurcated growth story, with overall headline numbers masking significant disparities across sectors. While new construction starts saw a 20% month-over-month decline in June after a 33.5% gain in May, this volatility is largely driven by a few massive projects in healthcare, manufacturing, utilities, and particularly data centers. Data centers and energy-related projects are primarily responsible for current construction growth, creating uneven backlogs for contractors, while residential and institutional sectors remain weak. The demand for design services, as indicated by the American Institute of Architects' Billings Index, suggests that broader nonresidential construction activity will likely remain soft into early 2027, highly sensitive to interest rate cuts and trade policy. Despite near-record employment levels, labor demand is concentrated in these high-growth segments, reinforcing the uneven distribution of activity across the industry.

articles.title: Forget Property Deeds: The Moon’s Real Estate Could Run on Operating Rights
articles.narrative: A Deloitte report, "Building the Lunar Economy," suggests that future commercial real estate on the Moon will operate under a system of operating rights and access rather than traditional property deeds due to the Outer Space Treaty. The report, informed by insights from industry leaders, highlights the eroding barriers to entry and growing promise of lunar resources, particularly at the South Pole, which is targeted by upcoming missions like NASA's Artemis Base Camp and China's International Lunar Research Station. Key infrastructure in transportation, power, communications, construction, and life support will be necessary to support commercial activity, with governments likely serving as initial anchor customers. While significant engineering and commercial viability challenges remain, the report emphasizes that the focus is shifting from whether humanity will return to the Moon to what happens once a sustained presence is established.

articles.title: Fifth Third Bank Expands Offices at 50 Rockefeller Plaza
articles.narrative: Fifth Third Bank has expanded its office presence at 50 Rockefeller Plaza, increasing its total footprint to 32,347 square feet. The expansion adds nearly 11,000 square feet to its existing lease, which now runs through February 2034. This growth reflects the bank's positive experience and continued commitment to the Rockefeller Center campus.

articles.title: Lincoln Property's New Pennsylvania Head On What Types Of Deals He's Targeting
articles.narrative: Lincoln Property's new Pennsylvania head, Charles McGrath, is prioritizing health, education, and residential conversion projects. This strategic focus indicates a shift towards sectors with strong demand drivers and opportunities for adaptive reuse within the state.

articles.title: America's Data Centers Are Running Out Of People Who Know How To Run Them
articles.narrative: The data center industry is facing significant labor shortages, especially for experienced senior leadership roles. This scarcity of skilled personnel is posing a challenge to the expansion of critical AI infrastructure, as operators struggle to find qualified individuals to manage and maintain these complex facilities.

articles.title: Houston-Area Manufactured Home Community Offering Units Below $90K
articles.narrative: Indigo Skies, a manufactured home community in Waller, is offering 439 units below $90,000. This development aims to address Houston's increasing demand for affordable housing, providing residents with resort-style amenities.

articles.title: Ruben Cos. Says It Can't Sell, Finance Navy Yard Multifamily Project
articles.narrative: Ruben Cos. is seeking an extension from the D.C. Zoning Commission for its approved plans to construct a 263-unit multifamily building near Nationals Park. The developer indicated that current market conditions, specifically high interest rates and construction costs, are making it difficult to secure financing or sell the project, necessitating more time to proceed with the development.

data_points.notable_features: Located one block from Nationals Park.
